novelty.basis: Introduces the basis-independent Quantum Christoffel Operator K_V (Def. 2.1), closed-form convex-hull mixing law with universal factor-of-2 sharpness on 2-tier semigroups (Thm. 2.2c), constant-free O(log^2 n) pure L^1->L^2 scaling (Thm. 3.1a), and global operator-order LDL^T gap/norm certification without L^dagger-invariance (Thm. 4.2).

reproducibility.basis: Provides complete Hamiltonian parameters, Table 1 manifest of 16 Lean 4 symbols (v4.35.0, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice), 8 pytest suites with 15 adversarial tamper checks, and 6 exact-Q certificates (14 linked LDL^T witnesses). rigor.basis: Non-asymptotic proofs of Eqs. (1)-(9), Schur-complement gap characterization (Thm. 2.1b), and Weyl/LDL^T soundness (Thm. 4.2) are complete. Rigor is tempered by Lean 4 covering only 16 discrete/algebraic cores over OrdField K (excluding matrix Holder and ODE comparison) and synthesis estimating delta_*^Q via float64 eigh(H).

significance.basis: Converts Chen-Ding's qualitative L^1->L^2 burn-in into an exact finite-size certification engine, yielding 1.26x-3.30x speedups on n<=4 TFIM/XXZ and 17.7x/20.7x on n=1000 depolarizing chains. Impact is bounded by O(d^6) dense LDL^T scaling for non-commuting chains and reliance on assumed linear lambda_k for O(log^2 n) scaling.

potential_errors: In Theorem 3.1(a)(i)-(ii), the explicit formula K_{V_k} = (\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{n}{j} 3^j) I and the Pauli-string KMS inner product identity require \sigma = I/2^n, which is stated in Section 2.1 (p. 3) and reflected by y_0 = 2^n - 1 but omitted inside the statement of Theorem 3.1(a)(i)-(ii).

Theorem 4.2 invokes an unquantized rational logarithm upper bound \log_\mathbb{Q}^{ub,exact} (and Table 1 lists geometric_tail_term_le), but the explicit rational formula/series used for \log_\mathbb{Q}^{ub,exact} is not printed in the manuscript text.

In Theorem 3.1(b), the heading calls it the 'Two-Regime \alpha-Super-Poincaré Phase Diagram' (referring to burn-in plus tail) while the text lists 'three exact non-vacuous regimes' (\alpha \in (0,1), \alpha = 1, \alpha > 1); additionally, the 5-qubit stabilizer code is written without double brackets as '5,1,3' (p. 5).
strengths: Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.1 establish a clean, basis-independent Quantum Christoffel Operator K_V and exact Quantum Super-Poincaré Inequality (Eq. 4) with a rigorous Schur-complement formula for \lambda_{op}(V^\perp) that coincides with \mu_{r+1} on \mathcal{L}^\dagger-invariant eigenmode subspaces.

Theorem 2.2 gives a completely closed-form piecewise-logarithmic mixing time T_{SP}(\varepsilon; y_0) across exact convex-hull knots y_j^* > C_{k_j}, proves strict speedup over T_{gap} for y_0 > y_1^*, and proves a sharp factor-of-2 plus O(1) optimality bound (Eq. 7) with T_{SP}/t_{exact} -> 1 in both \varepsilon -> 0^+ and y_0 -> \infty limits.

Theorem 3.1(a) proves an explicit, constant-free O(\log^2 n) mixing bound (Eq. 8) from pure L^1 -> L^2 projection without hypercontractivity (with universal c=3 and product-state c=1, matching the 22.82 cap at n=1,000), and Theorem 3.1(b) gives exact closed-form decay across \alpha \in (0,1), \alpha=1, and \alpha > 1.

Theorems 4.1 and 4.2 lift the envelope to trace-norm and sandwiched Rényi-2/relative-entropy bounds (Eq. 9) and establish sound exact-\mathbb{Q} LDL^\top certification via penalty-shifted operator inequalities and Weyl bounds without requiring \mathcal{L}^\dagger-invariance.

All numerical values in Table 2, Figures 1-3, and Section 6 (including 2-tier sharpness ratios 1.045-1.145 and T_{gap} calculations) are internally consistent, and limitations (float64 eigh(H) radius estimation in synthesis, O(d^6) scaling, and eigenmode vs. Pauli filtrations) are transparently disclosed.
strong_novelty_candidates: Basis-independent Quantum Christoffel Operator K_V = \sum_{a=1}^D E_a^\dagger E_a and its exact Quantum Spectral Christoffel-Super-Poincaré Inequality (Theorem 2.1).

Closed-form upper-convex-hull piecewise-logarithmic mixing law with universal factor-of-2 optimality on 2-tier semigroups (Theorem 2.2) and constant-free O(\log^2 n) pure L^1 -> L^2 bound without hypercontractivity (Theorem 3.1a).
Penalty-shifted global operator-order exact-\mathbb{Q} LDL^\top certification of higher-tier subspace gaps and Christoffel norms (Theorem 4.2).
summary: The manuscript converts Chen and Ding's qualitative L^1 -> L^2 rapid-mixing mechanism into an exact, non-asymptotic mixing-time certification framework for KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups. It introduces the basis-independent Quantum Christoffel Operator K_V, proves a Quantum Super-Poincaré Inequality with an exact Schur-complement subspace gap (Theorem 2.1), integrates the upper convex hull into a closed-form piecewise-logarithmic mixing time with factor-of-2 optimality on 2-tier semigroups (Theorem 2.2), derives a constant-free O(\log^2 n) mixing bound without hypercontractivity alongside an \alpha-Super-Poincaré phase diagram (Theorem 3.1), lifts convex-hull bounds to trace-norm and relative-entropy decay (Theorem 4.1), and constructs exact-\mathbb{Q} LDL^\top certificates on quantized operator bundles conditioned on perturbation radii \delta_*^\mathbb{Q} (Theorem 4.2), supported by 16 zero-dependency Lean 4 algebraic lemmas and benchmarks on 1D TFIM/XXZ (n<=4) and depolarizing chains (n<=1,000). All mathematical derivations, inequalities, and numerical tables checked in the PDF are sound and internally consistent, with limitations honestly disclosed.
weaknesses: For non-commuting interacting spin chains, the paper does not prove analytical lower bounds on \lambda_{op}(V_k^\perp) for Pauli-weight subspaces as n -> \infty; instead, Experiment 1 and the exact-\mathbb{Q} LDL^\top certificates use the exact \mathcal{L}^\dagger-invariant eigenmode filtration V_r, limiting dense LDL^\top certification to n <= 4 due to O(d^6) = O(2^{6n}) complexity, while O(\log^2 n) scaling is demonstrated only under assumed linear \lambda_k on commuting depolarizing semigroups.

For the two interacting-chain LDL^\top certificates (n=2 TFIM and XXZ), the synthesis script estimates the Frobenius perturbation radii \delta_*^\mathbb{Q} against float64 eigh(H) outputs rather than interval-certified eigensolvers, so end-to-end floating-point-free provenance from H is achieved only for the analytical depolarizing certificates (n=50, 100), not yet for interacting Hamiltonians.

The Lean 4 formalization over OrdField K covers 16 finite-dimensional algebraic and discrete-vector core lemmas (e.g., discrete probability vector trace_norm_sq_le_chi2 and quadratic form positivity ldlt_quad_nonneg), leaving the non-commutative matrix Hölder step (Eq. 3), continuous-time ODE comparison, and Theorem 3.1 integral comparisons unformalized in Lean.
